items.name: Binary n-ic forms ordered by height
items.statement: V_n = Sym^n(2) is the space of binary n-ic forms f(x, y) = a_0x^n + a_1x^{n−1}y + ⋯ + a_ny^n, with SL_2 acting by γ·f(x, y) = f((x, y)·γ). The height is H(f) = max{|a_0|, …, |a_n|}, so #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X} = (2X)^{n+1} + O(X^n).
items.locator: §1, p.2; §3, p.7; Theorem 6, p.4, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The discriminant of a binary form
items.statement: Δ(f) is the homogeneous polynomial of degree 2n − 2 in the coefficients of f whose nonvanishing means that f has n distinct linear factors over an algebraic closure; Δ(xf) = Δ(f)·f(0, 1)².
items.note: Mathlib 082e2d3 has Polynomial.discr (RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean:930) for f(x, 1), which agrees with Δ(f) when a_0 ≠ 0; the homogeneous binary-form discriminant, valid also when a_0 = 0, is not there. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Stickelberger for binary forms: 2 | Δ implies 4 | Δ
items.statement: For every integral binary form f, Δ(f) ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4). Hence if 2 | Δ(f) then 4 | Δ(f + 2g) for every g, so 4 always divides strongly and W^{(2)}_m = ∅ for even m.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, subset 3, pp.54–55 ("if p = 2, then since 2 | Δ(f), we have 4 | Δ(f)"), Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (gap E6)
items.note: Checked for all forms mod 4 of degree n ≤ 5. Tau Ceti has the number-field version (TauCeti.NumberField.discr_emod_four_eq_zero_or_one, NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean:104 at f790474), not this one. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The rank-n ring R_f of a binary form (Birch–Merriman, Nakagawa, Wood)
items.statement: For f with a_0 ≠ 0, let θ be the image of x in K_f = Q[x]/(f(x, 1)). R_f is the Z-module spanned by 1, a_0θ, a_0θ² + a_1θ, …, a_0θ^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_{n−1}θ. It is closed under multiplication, and disc(R_f) = Δ(f). The subscheme of P¹_Z cut out by f is regular iff R_f is maximal.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Strong and weak divisibility for binary forms; W^{(1)}_m, W^{(2)}_m
items.statement: For a prime p and f with p² | Δ(f), p² strongly divides Δ(f) if p² | Δ(f + pg) for every integral binary n-ic form g, and weakly otherwise. For squarefree m > 0, W^{(1)}_m (resp. W^{(2)}_m) is the set of forms whose discriminant is strongly (resp. weakly) divisible by p² for every p | m; W_m is the set of forms with m² | Δ(f). For odd p, p² strongly divides Δ(f) iff f mod p has a factor h³ with h linear or j² with deg j ≥ 2.
items.locator: §1, p.3; Appendix, p.54; §6.5, p.50, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Densities ν_0(n, p), ν_1(n, p) of v_p(Δ) = 0, 1 for monic polynomials (corrected)
items.statement: Among monic degree-n polynomials over Z_p, the density with p ∤ Δ is ν_0(n, p) = 1 − 1/p for n ≥ 2 (1 for n = 1). The density with v_p(Δ) = 1 is ν_1(n, p) = 0 for p = 2 or n = 1; p^{−1}(1 − p^{−1}) for n = 2; and (1 − p^{−1})²(1 − (−p)^{2−n})/(1 + p) for n ≥ 3 (for n = 3 this is p^{−1}(1 − p^{−1})²). The paper quotes (1 − (−p)^{−n}) for n ≥ 4 (E1).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, p.53, citing [2, Proposition 6.4 and Theorem 6.8], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E1)
items.note: ν_0 + ν_1 must equal the density λ_n(p) of p² ∤ Δ (Yamamura; PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22), and the corrected ν_1 does. For p = 3, n = 4: λ_4(3) = 62/81 by exhaustive count, so ν_1(4, 3) = 8/81, while the printed formula gives 80/729. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition A.1 (density α_n(p) of p² ∤ Δ for binary forms; corrected)
items.statement: α_2(2) = 1/2 and α_n(2) = 3/8 for n ≥ 3. For odd p, α_n(p) = (1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p − 1/p³) for n = 2; (1 − 1/p)²(1 + 1/p)² for n = 3; and (1 − 1/p)²(1 + 1/p)(1 + 1/p − 1/p²) = (1 − 1/p)²(1 + 2/p − 1/p³) for every n ≥ 4. The printed n = 4 value (1 − 1/p)²(1 + 2/p − 2/p⁴ + 1/p⁵) is wrong (E1). The proof splits forms by p ∤ a_0; p | a_0, p ∤ a_1; and p | a_0, a_1, using Δ(a_0x^n + ⋯) ≡ −4a_0a_2³Δ(a_2x^{n−2} + ⋯) mod (a_0², a_0a_1, a_1²).
items.locator: Proposition A.1 and proof, pp.53–55, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E1)
items.note: Exhaustive counts mod p²: α_n(2) for n = 2, …, 5; α_2, α_3, α_4 at p = 3; α_2, α_3, α_4 at p = 5; α_5 at p = 3. All match the corrected formulas; α_4(3) = 176/243 and α_4(5) = 2784/3125 contradict the printed n = 4 formula. The congruence was checked symbolically for n = 3, …, 6. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition A.2 (density β_n(p) of p-maximal R_f)
items.statement: β_2(p) = (1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p − 1/p³) and β_n(p) = (1 − 1/p²)(1 − 1/p³) for n ≥ 3. Proof: Hensel-factor f = h_1h_2 with h_1 ≡ y^k (mod p) and h_2 monic; R_{h_1} is maximal iff k ≤ 1 or p² ∤ the x^k-coefficient; h_2 is maximal with probability 1 − p^{−2} (Lenstra, [2, Proposition 3.5]).
items.locator: Proposition A.2 and proof, p.55, citing [2, Proposition 3.5], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Checked by exhaustive count over f mod p² (maximality via v_p(Δ) = v_p(d_K) with PARI) for (n, p) = (2, 2), (3, 2), (4, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Lenstra: monic polynomials are p-maximal with density 1 − p^{−2}
items.statement: For n ≥ 2 and every prime p, the density of monic degree-n polynomials over Z_p with Z_p[x]/(f) maximal is 1 − p^{−2} ([2, Proposition 3.5]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.2, p.55, citing [2], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: The same statement is an item of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22 (routed to ST.0); coalesce. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The representation W_n = 2 ⊗ Sym²(n) of SL_2 × SL_n
items.statement: W_n is the space of pairs (A, B) of symmetric n × n matrices, with (γ_2, γ_n)·(A, B) = (γ_nAγ_n^t, γ_nBγ_n^t)·γ_2^t. The invariant binary form is f_{A,B}(x, y) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}det(Ax − By) (1); Δ(A, B) := Δ(f_{A,B}) and H(A, B) := H(f_{A,B}).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The SL_n-invariant ring of W_n
items.statement: The ring of SL_n(C)-invariant polynomials on W_n(C) is freely generated by the coefficients of the invariant binary n-ic form.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Arithmetic invariant theory of W_n for odd n (Bhargava–Gross–Wang)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1, k a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f ∈ V(k) with Δ(f) ≠ 0 and a_0 ≠ 0, C_f : z² = f(x, y)y ⊂ P(1, 1, g + 1) and J_f its Jacobian. The stabilizer of any (A, B) with f_{A,B} = f is ≅ J_f[2](k); SL_n(k)-orbits with invariant form f inject into H¹(k, J_f[2]). (A, B) is distinguished if Δ ≠ 0 and A, B have a common isotropic g-dimensional k-subspace; distinguished orbits map to the identity, and their isotropic subspaces are in bijection with J_f[2](k).
items.locator: §3.1, p.7, citing [7], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The subspace W_0, its parabolic G_0 and the space U_g
items.statement: For n = 2g + 1, W_0 ⊂ W is the subspace of pairs whose top left g × g blocks vanish, in block form (2), and G_0 ⊂ SL_n is the maximal parabolic preserving Y_g = ⟨e_1, …, e_g⟩, in block form (3) with γ_1 ∈ GL_g, γ_2 ∈ GL_{g+1}. G_0 acts on the top right g × (g + 1) blocks by (γ_1A^topγ_2^t, γ_1B^topγ_2^t), giving the space U_g = 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1), on which the unipotent radical acts trivially. Every distinguished element of W(k) is SL_n(k)-equivalent to an element of W_0(k).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Existence and number of orbits for even n
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2, f ∈ V(k) with Δ(f) ≠ 0 and a_0 ≠ 0, L = k[x]/(f(x, 1)), and V_f(k) = {(A, B) ∈ W_n(k) : f_{A,B} = f}. Then V_f(k) ≠ ∅ iff a_0 ∈ k^{×2}N_{L/k}(L^×) ([8, Theorem 7]); for instance V_f(R) = ∅ for negative definite f. Over a finite field of odd characteristic, V_f(k) ≠ ∅ and the SL_n(k)-orbits correspond to the even-degree factorizations of f.
items.locator: §3.1, p.8, citing [8, Theorem 7], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (U_g is prehomogeneous)
items.statement: The representation U_g of G_m × H_g, H_g = SL_2 × SL_g × SL_{g+1}, has a single Zariski-open orbit, and the stabilizer in H_g(C) of a point of it is ≅ SL_2(C). Proof: induction on g; U_g is a castling transform of U_{g−1} (Sato–Kimura), and castling preserves open orbits, generic stabilizers and relative invariants. Hence the H_g-invariant ring is generated by one irreducible polynomial.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 and proof, p.8, citing [30, §2], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: AnalyticNumberTheory AN.8 plans prehomogeneous zeta functions, but not the Sato–Kimura algebra itself. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The Q-invariant (hyperdeterminant of format 2 × g × (g + 1))
items.statement: For (A^top, B^top) ∈ U_g, let f_i(x, y) = (−1)^{i+1}det(A_ix − B_iy), where A_i, B_i delete the i-th column, and let C be the (g + 1) × (g + 1) matrix of their coefficients. Q := det C is the hyperdeterminant of (A^top, B^top) ([18, Ch. 14, Theorem 3.18]), irreducible of degree g(g + 1), and it generates the invariant ring. On W_0, Q(A, B) := Q(A^top, B^top) (4) and Q(γ·(A, B)) = det(γ_1)^{g+1}det(γ_2)^gQ(A, B) = det(γ_1)Q(A, B) (5), so |Q| is G_0(Z)-invariant.
items.note: The same invariant, with A^top fixed, is an item of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22; coalesce. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4 (the locus Q = 0)
items.statement: Let Y ⊂ Z ⊂ W_0, where Z = {Δ = 0} and Y is the locus where f_{A,B} is divisible by the cube of a form of degree ≥ 1 or the square of a form of degree ≥ 2. Then the generic element mod Q is not in Y(R/(Q)) (Proposition 3.2). For (A^top, B^top) of the shape (6), Q = ±a_1^ga_2^{g−1}⋯a_gb_1b_2²⋯b_g^g (Lemma 3.3). Every (A, B) ∈ W_0(k) ∖ Y(k) with Q(A, B) = 0 is SL_2(k) × G_0(k)-equivalent to a pair whose top blocks have the normal form (7), with a_1, …, a_g, b_2, …, b_g ≠ 0 (Proposition 3.4).
items.locator: Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.4 and proofs, pp.9–11, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.5 (Q² divides Δ on W_0)
items.statement: Q² | Δ in Z[W_0]. Proof: Propositions 3.2 and 3.4 show that Q | Δ, and a first-order deformation in the (1, n − 1)-entry of B shows that Q also divides Δ/Q.
items.locator: Theorem 3.5 and proof, p.11, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Checked at 37–40 random integral points of W_0 for n = 3 and 5. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (corrected: Δ lies in the ideal of maximal minors of B^top and of A^top)
items.statement: Δ vanishes on W_0(C) wherever A^top or B^top has rank < g (a kernel vector of B in ⟨e_1, …, e_g⟩ is A-isotropic). Hence Δ lies in the ideal generated by the g × g minors of B^top (a prime determinantal ideal), and likewise for A^top. On bounded sets this gives |Δ| ≪ det(B^top(B^top)^t)^{1/2}. The printed statement, det(A^top(A^top)^t)det(B^top(B^top)^t) | Δ in Z[W_0], is false (E2).
items.locator: Proposition 3.6 and proof, pp.11–12, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E2)
items.note: For n = 3, det(A^topA^topᵗ)det(B^topB^topᵗ) divided Δ at only 6 of 37 random integral points; an explicit counterexample is in E2. The vanishing on rank-deficient B^top was checked at 12 random points for n = 5. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The embedding σ_m for odd n: normal form (8) and matrices (9)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1 and m > 0 odd squarefree. For f ∈ W^{(2)}_m there is γ ∈ SL_2(Z) with f((x, y)γ) = m²b_0x^n + mb_1x^{n−1}y + ⋯ + b_ny^n and (m, b_0) = 1 (8). The pair (A, B) of (9), with antidiagonal 1s in A, m in the positions shown, c_0 = b_0 and r chosen with m | 2rc_0 + b_1, has (−1)^gdet(xA − yB) = f((x, y)γ) for suitable integers c_i, found inductively. σ_m(f) = (A_f, B_f) is defined by (A_f, −B_f)^t = γ^{−1}(A, −B)^t.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.7 (σ_m for odd n)
items.statement: For odd squarefree m > 0 (the statement omits "odd", E10) there is a map σ_m : W^{(2)}_m → W_0(Z) with f_{σ_m(f)} = f and |Q|(σ_m(f)) = m.
items.locator: Theorem 3.7, p.12, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: |Q| on distinguished pairs with an isotropic lattice
items.statement: For distinguished (A, B) ∈ W(Z) with a common isotropic g-dimensional subspace X, let Λ = X ∩ Z^n. There is γ ∈ SL_n(Z), unique up to G_0(Z), with Λ = γ^t⟨e_1, …, e_g⟩_Z; then |Q|(A, B, Λ) := |Q|(γ·(A, B)). W(Z)^{dist,irr}_{|Q|>M} is the set of distinguished elements with irreducible invariant form and |Q| > M.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.8 (uniqueness of the isotropic lattice)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1 ≥ 3, m odd positive squarefree, and f ∈ W^{(2)}_m irreducible. Every (A, B) ∈ SL_n(Z)·σ_m(f) has a unique primitive g-dimensional isotropic lattice Λ, and |Q|(A, B, Λ) = m. So σ_m(f) and σ_{m′}(f) are not SL_n(Z)-equivalent for distinct m, m′. Proof: J_f[2](Q) = 1 for irreducible f.
items.locator: Proposition 3.8 and proof, p.13, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The embedding for even n via xf, and the set W^{(2),gen}_{m,n}
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2 and m odd squarefree. W^{(2),gen}_{m,n} ⊂ W^{(2)}_{m,n} consists of the f with f(0, 1) coprime to m. Since Δ(xf) = Δ(f)f(0, 1)², xf ∈ W^{(2)}_{m,n+1}, and σ_{m,n}(f) := σ_{m,n+1}(xf) ∈ W_{n+1}(Z). Its B is singular, with a 1-dimensional kernel that is not A-isotropic.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The q-invariant on W_1
items.statement: W_1(D) ⊂ W(D) (for W = W_{n+1}) consists of pairs with the top left (g + 1) × (g + 1) block of A and the top left (g + 2) × (g + 2) block of B zero, and ker B 1-dimensional and not A-isotropic. With B′ the (nonsingular) top right (g + 1) × (g + 1) block of B, det(B′) | Q(A^top, B^top), and q(A, B) := Q(A^top, B^top)/det(B′) (10). For γ ∈ G_1 in block form (11), q(γ(A, B)) = det(γ_1)γ_2q(A, B) (12). For distinguished (A, B) with B singular, a common isotropic (g + 1)-space X and X′ = X + ker B give |q|(A, B, Λ, Λ′).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.9 (|Q| and |q| of σ_m(f), n even)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2, m odd positive squarefree and f ∈ W^{(2),gen}_m irreducible. For (A, B) ∈ SL_{n+1}(Z)·σ_m(f) and a (g + 1)-dimensional primitive A-isotropic Λ inside a (g + 2)-dimensional primitive B-isotropic Λ′, |Q|(A, B, Λ) ∈ {m, |f(0, 1)|m} and |q|(A, B, Λ, Λ′) = m. There are exactly two such Λ (#J_{xf}[2](Q) = 2), the second the A-reflection of the first in e_{n+1}^⊥. Distinct m give inequivalent σ_m(f).
items.locator: Proposition 3.9 and proof, pp.14–15, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Kuba: reducible binary forms are O(X^n)
items.statement: The number of reducible f ∈ V_n(Z) with H(f) < X is O(X^n) ([22, Theorem 1]).
items.note: Routed to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2 as a source.

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility: 100% of binary forms have Galois group S_n
items.statement: When ordered by height, 100% of integral binary n-ic forms are irreducible with Gal(f(x, 1)) = S_n; the set V(Z)^red = {f : Gal(f(x, 1)) ≠ S_n} (31) is negligible.
items.note: IG.2 plans Hilbert irreducibility. The paper needs a power-saving count; see E7.

items.name: Iwasawa decomposition and Siegel sets for SL_n(Z)\SL_n(R)
items.statement: SL_n(R) = NTK with N lower unipotent, K = SO(n) and T the positive diagonal torus, and a fundamental set F for SL_n(Z) on SL_n(R) inside a Siegel set N′T′K with s_i ≥ c.
items.note: AA.3 plans Siegel sets and the finite covering of arithmetic quotients.

items.name: Reduction to torus integrals for odd n
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1 and Y = X^{1/n}. With s_i = (t_i/t_{i+1})^{1/n}, δ(s) = ∏_{i<j}t_j/t_i = ∏_ks_k^{−nk(n−k)}, R′ = σ_1(W(1)), R = R_{>0}·R′ (every distinguished real element is SL_n(R)-equivalent into R) and B ⊃ H_0·R′ bounded, the number of SL_n(Z)-orbits on an SL_n(Z)-invariant L ⊂ W(Z) of real-distinguished elements of height < X is ≪ ∫_{s_i≥c}#(s(YB) ∩ L)δ(s)d^×s =: I_X(L) (16). By (14) (Kuba), the left side of Theorem 5(b) is ≪ #SL_n(Z)∖W(Z)^{dist,irr}_{|Q|>M, H<X} + O(X^n). w(a_ij) = w(b_ij) = t_i^{−1}t_j^{−1}, and w(Q) = ∏_{k≤g}t_k^{−1} (15). I_X splits into the main body, the shallow cusp and the deep cusp (17).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (Davenport's lemma)
items.statement: Let R ⊂ R^n be a bounded semialgebraic multiset of maximal multiplicity m, defined by at most k polynomial inequalities of degree ≤ ℓ, and R′ its image under a triangular unipotent transformation. Then #(R′ ∩ Z^n) = Vol(R) + O(max{Vol(R̄), 1}), where Vol(R̄) is the largest volume of a coordinate projection of R, with the constant depending only on n, m, k and ℓ ([14]).
items.locator: Proposition 4.1, p.17, citing [14], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.3 (the large sieve in boxes)
items.statement: For Ω_p ⊂ V(F_p) with ω(p) = #Ω_p/#V(F_p) and a box B′ with sides X_1, …, X_N, the set S of v ∈ V(Z) ∩ B′ with v mod p ∉ Ω_p for all p satisfies |S| ≤ ∏(X_i^{1/2} + L)²·(Σ_{m<L squarefree}∏_{p|m}ω(p)/(1 − ω(p)))^{−1} for every L > 0 (18). If ω(p) ≫ 1, then |S| ≪_{n,ε} X_1⋯X_N/min{X_i}^{1/2−ε}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3 and proof, p.18, citing [19, Theorem 1], [23, Proposition 2.4], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: The remark that the large sieve would improve Shankar–Tsimerman's quintic error term to X^{159/160+ε} is not proved. Routed to SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2 as a source.

items.name: Non-distinguished elements have p-adic density bounded below
items.statement: The density of non-F_p-distinguished elements of W(F_p) is bounded below by a positive constant independent of p ([20, Proposition 4.6]).
items.locator: §4.2, pp.17–18, citing [20], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.4 (main body, odd n)
items.statement: I^main_X(W(Z)^dist) ≪_ε X^{n+1−1/(2n)+ε}. Proof: the large sieve with Ω_p the non-distinguished classes, using w(a_11)^{−1/2}δ(s) = ∏s_k^{(1−nk)(n−k)} ≪ 1.
items.locator: Proposition 4.4 and proof, p.18, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.5 (shallow cusp, odd n)
items.statement: I^scusp_X(W(Z)) ≪ X^{n+1−1/n}, by the proof of [20, Proposition 4.3].
items.locator: Proposition 4.5, p.19, citing [20], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 4.6–4.7 (vanishing discriminant and the cutoff s_i ≪ X^Θ)
items.statement: If a_ij = b_ij = 0 for all i ≤ k, j ≤ n − k (some k ≤ g), then f_{A,B} has a square factor of degree k and Δ(A, B) = 0 (Lemma 4.6). Hence there is Θ = Θ(n) such that s(YB) ∩ W(Z) contains only points of discriminant 0 when some s_i ≫ X^Θ: nonvanishing forces t_kt_{n−k} ≪ Y for k ≤ g, so t_n ≫ Y^{−g} (Lemma 4.7).
items.locator: Lemmas 4.6–4.7 and proofs, p.19, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.8 (deep cusp, odd n)
items.statement: I^dcusp_X(W(Z)^irr_{|Q|>M}) ≪_ε X^{n+1+ε}/M. Proof: for saturated Z ⊂ U_0 ∩ U′ (U′ = {i + j < n}), bound ∏_{α∈U_0∖Z}Yw(α) by (19) × ∏_{α∈Z}Yw(π(α))/Yw(α) (20), with π(a_ij) = a_{i,n−i}, π(b_ij) = b_{n−j,j}. Their product is Y^{n(n+1)}/(Y^{g(g+1)}w(Q)) times all t_i/t_j except those with i ≥ g + 1, j = n. So it is ≪ Y^{n(n+1)}δ(s)^{−1}/M.
items.locator: Proposition 4.8 and proof, pp.19–20, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprints E10)
items.note: The products (19)–(20) were checked symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3. The printed second factor of (20) must run over 1 ≤ i < j ≤ g. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.2 (tail count, odd n)
items.statement: I_X(W(Z)^{dist,irr}_{|Q|>M}) ≪_ε X^{n+1−1/(2n)+ε} + X^{n+1+ε}/M, from Propositions 4.4, 4.5 and 4.8.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2, p.17, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (Schmidt's lattice-point bound)
items.statement: For a rank-k lattice Λ ⊂ R^m with successive minima μ_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ μ_k and a bounded open D ⊂ R^m, #(YD ∩ Λ) = O(max_{1≤j≤k}Y^j/(μ_1⋯μ_j)) ([31]).
items.locator: Proposition 5.2, p.22, citing [31], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Singular symmetric matrices in skew balls; S(Λ), ℓ_i ∗ ℓ_j, C(r, s)
items.statement: S = Sym²(n) with the Euclidean length, S(Z)^{(r)} the rank-r integral matrices, s = diag(t_1^{−1}, …, t_n^{−1}) ∈ T′ with Y^{−Θ} ≪ t_n ≤ t_1 ≪ Y^Θ, and N_r(Y, s) = #(s(YD) ∩ S(Z)^{(r)}). C(r, s) = ∏_{i≤r}∏_{j≤n−i}t_j/t_{n−i+1} = ∏_{i<j, j>n−r}t_i/t_j ≪ δ(s)^{−1} (21). For a primitive rank-r Λ ⊂ Z^n, S(Λ) is the set of B ∈ S(Z) whose row space is a full-rank sublattice of Λ ⊗ R, and S′(Λ) is the lattice it spans. v_1 ∗ v_2 = v_1v_2^t + v_2v_1^t (or v_1v_2^t if they are dependent), with |v||w| ≤ |v ∗ w| ≤ 2|v||w| (24).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5.3 and Propositions 5.4–5.5 (Eskin–Katznelson lattices)
items.statement: For γ ∈ SL_n(R) and a basis ℓ_1, …, ℓ_r of γΛ, {ℓ_i ∗ ℓ_j : i ≤ j} is a basis of γ(S′(Λ)), with d(γS′(Λ)) = 2^{r(r−1)/4}d(γΛ)^{r+1}, and it is almost reduced if {ℓ_i} is. If YD ∩ γS(Λ) ≠ ∅ then μ_iμ_j ≤ c_1Y for i + j ≤ r + 1 (Proposition 5.4). And #(YD ∩ γS(Λ)) = O(Y^{r(r+1)/2}d(Λ)^{−(r+1)}∏_{i<j, i+j≤r+1}μ_j/μ_i) (Proposition 5.5, (25)).
items.locator: Theorem 5.3, Propositions 5.4–5.5 and proofs, pp.22–23, citing [17, Proposition 3.3, Lemmas 3.5 and 4.1], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7 (counting the row lattices)
items.statement: If some primitive rank-r Λ has s^{−1}Λ with successive minima in [L_i, 2L_i), then L_it_j^{−1} > c′ whenever i + j ≥ n + 1 (Lemma 5.6), and #Σ(L, s) = O((L_1⋯L_r)^n∏_{i<j}(L_i/L_j)·C(r, s)) (Proposition 5.7, (28)).
items.locator: Lemma 5.6, Proposition 5.7 and proofs, pp.23–24, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (singular symmetric matrices in skew balls)
items.statement: For n ≥ 2, 1 ≤ r < n, Θ > 0, Y > 1 and s ∈ T′ with t_1 ≪ Y^Θ, t_n ≫ Y^{−Θ}: N_r(Y, s) = O(C(r, s)Y^{nr/2}log^rY), uniformly in s. For s = 1 this follows from Eskin–Katznelson [17]; the proof sums Proposition 5.5 over dyadic ranges of successive minima using Proposition 5.7.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1 and proof, pp.21, 24–25, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10)
items.note: A simplified Eskin–Katznelson upper bound in skewed domains, at the cost of log factors. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 as a source.

items.name: Auxiliary sets for even n and the containment (35)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 2, V = V_n, W = W_{n+1}, m odd squarefree and a small κ > 0: V(Z)^red = {Gal(f(x, 1)) ≠ S_n} (31); V(Z)^{Δ small} = {|Δ(f)| ≤ H(f)^{2n−2−κ}} (32, printed without the absolute value); W^{(1#)}_m = {f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : m | f(0, 1)} (33); W^gen_m = {f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : (m, f(0, 1)) = 1, f ∉ V^red ∪ V^{Δ small}} (34). Then ⋃_{m>M}W^{(2)}_m ⊂ V^red ∪ V^{Δ small} ∪ ⋃_{m>√M}W^{(1#)}_m ∪ ⋃_{m>√M}W^gen_m (35). L(M) = ⋃_{m>M}SL_{n+1}(Z)·σ_m(W^gen_m), and (36) ≪ I_X(L(M)) with Y = X^{1/(n+1)} (37).
items.locator: §6, (31)–(37), pp.25–26, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10, gap E7)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 6.1 (forms with small discriminant)
items.statement: The number of integral binary n-ic forms of height < X and |Δ| < X^{2n−2−κ} is O(X^{n+1−κ/(2n−2)}). Proof: for |a_0| > X^{1−η}, Δ is a degree-(n − 1) polynomial in a_n with leading coefficient C_na_0^{n−1}, so a_n lies within X^{1−η} of one of its roots.
items.locator: Lemma 6.1 and proof, p.25, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (the set W^{(1#)}_m)
items.statement: #⋃_{m>√M}{f ∈ W^{(1#)}_m : H(f) < X} = O(X^{n+1}/√M + X^n), by the quantitative Ekedahl sieve ([4, Theorem 3.3]), since p | f(0, 1) together with p² | Δ is a codimension-2 condition mod p.
items.locator: Lemma 6.2, p.26, citing [4], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Bhargava's quantitative Ekedahl sieve ([4, Theorem 3.3])
items.statement: For a closed subscheme Y ⊂ A^N_Z of codimension k ≥ 2 and a bounded region B, #{a ∈ rB ∩ Z^N : a mod p ∈ Y(F_p) for some p > M} = O(r^N/(M^{k−1}log M) + r^{N−k+1}). This gives Theorem 5(a) and Lemma 6.2.
items.locator: Theorem 5(a), p.3; §6.5, p.50; Lemma 6.2, p.26, citing [4], [16], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Also an item of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22 and PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21 (both routed to ST.2); coalesce. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Fibering the count over row spaces of the singular B
items.statement: For a primitive rank-n Λ ⊂ Z^{n+1}, S(Λ) is the lattice of B ∈ S(Z) with row space in Λ; Σ(L, s) are those Λ with successive minima of s^{−1}Λ in [L_i, 2L_i], and S(L, s) = ⋃_{Λ∈Σ(L,s)}S(Λ). The coordinates ℓ_ij of a reduced basis have weights w_L(ℓ_ij) = L_it_j^{−1}. Saturated sets Z ⊂ K ∪ M, the regions T_Z(L, Y) (38) and N(L, L, Z, X) (39) give I_X(L(M)) ≪ Σ_LΣ_ZN(L(M), L, Z, X), with the main body (a_11 ∉ Z), the shallow cusp (a_11 ∈ Z, a_{g+1,g+1} ∉ Z) and the deep cusp (a_{g+1,g+1} ∈ Z) (40).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 6.3 (preliminary bound)
items.statement: For saturated Z, N(L(1), L, Z, X) ≪ X^{n+1}∫_{T_Z(L,Y)}Y^{−#(Z∩K)}w(Z)^{−1}(∏_{i<j, i+j>n+1}L_i/L_j)δ(s)d^×s (41), by Davenport for the A's (42) and (43)–(44) for the B's.
items.locator: Proposition 6.3 and proof, p.28, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.4–6.5 (conditions forcing Δ = 0)
items.statement: Δ(A, B) = 0 if (a) dim ker B ≥ 2; (b) some nonzero v ∈ ker B is A-isotropic; or (c) a_ij = b_ij = 0 for i ≤ k, j ≤ n + 1 − k for some k ≤ g + 1 (Lemma 6.4). Hence N(L(1), L, Z, X) = 0 if Z ⊄ Z_1 = {a_ij : i + j ≤ n} ∪ {ℓ_ij : i + j ≤ n + 1}, or if a_kk, ℓ_{n+1−k,k} ∈ Z for some k ≤ g + 1 (Lemma 6.5).
items.locator: Lemmas 6.4–6.5 and proofs, p.29, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 6.7 and Corollary 6.8 (non-distinguished A for a fixed singular B_0)
items.statement: For B_0 ∈ S(F_p) of rank n, the set S^ndist_{B_0}(F_p) of A with Δ(A, B_0) ≠ 0 and no common isotropic (g + 1)-space has density ≫_n 1 in S(F_p). The same holds with a_11 = a ∈ F_p^× fixed, relative to #S(F_p)/p. Proof: completely split forms xf lift to nondistinguished pairs, and the orbit-stabilizer theorem applies with #G_{B_0}(F_p) = p^n·#O(b_0)(F_p) = 2p^{(n²+n)/2}(1 − O(p^{−2})).
items.locator: Lemma 6.7, Corollary 6.8 and proofs, pp.30–31, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 6.9 (main body, B with zero first row)
items.statement: ∫_{Yw(a_11)≫1}#{(A, B) ∈ (s(YD) × s(YD)) ∩ L(1) : b_{1i} = 0 ∀i}δ(s)d^×s ≪ X^{n+1−1/(4n)+ε} (45), by fibering over a_11 and the large sieve on a_12 (46).
items.locator: Proposition 6.9, Remark 6.10 and proof, pp.31–32, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: The exponent bookkeeping in (46) was checked. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.6 (main body, even n; corrected exponent)
items.statement: I^main_X(L(1)) = O(X^{n+1−θ_n+ε}) with θ_n = min{1/(4n), (n − 2)/(2n² + 2n + 2)}, which is 1/(4n) for n ≥ 6 and 1/21 for n = 4. The printed exponent 1/(4n) is not reached for n = 4 (E4). Proof: Proposition 6.9, plus a split of s_n at Y^δ into (47) and (48), with δ = (n + 3/2)/(n² + n + 1).
items.locator: Theorem 6.6 and proof, pp.29–33, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E4)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.12–6.14 (the preliminary shallow-cusp bound O_ε(X^{n+1+ε}))
items.statement: With the maps π_k and Z* of §6.3.1, (∏_{α∈Z*}w(π_k(α))/w(α))δ(s) = 1 (49). For saturated Z ⊂ Z_1 with a_11 ∈ Z, a_{g+1,g+1} ∉ Z and k maximal with a_kk ∈ Z, π_k(α) ∉ Z (Lemma 6.13), and (∏_{α∈Z}w(π_k(α))/w(α))(∏L_i/L_j)δ(s) ≪ 1 (50). Hence N(L(M), L, Z, X) ≪_ε X^{n+1+ε}.
items.locator: §6.3.1, Lemmas 6.12–6.14 and proofs, pp.33–35, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.15–6.17 and Proposition 6.18 (shallow cusp, Z ∩ K_1 ≠ K_1)
items.statement: With K_1 = {a_1j : j ≤ g + 2} and I(Z′, s) as in Lemma 6.15, the integrand of (41) is ≪ I(Z ∩ K_1, s) (Lemma 6.15). If Z ∩ K_1 ≠ K_1 and I ≫ Y^{−2δ}, then s_n ≫ Y^{1/2−δ} (Lemma 6.16). There #(s(YD) × s(YD)) ∩ W(Z)·δ(s) ≪ Y^{(n/2+2)(n+1)+n(2n²+9n+9)δ} (Lemma 6.17). With δ = (n − 2)/(4n² + 14n + 4) this gives N(L(M), L, Z, X) ≪ X^{n+1−(n−2)/(2(n+1)(n²+7n+7))} (Proposition 6.18).
items.locator: §6.3.2–6.3.3, Lemmas 6.15–6.17, Proposition 6.18 and proofs, pp.35–39, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: The δ-balance of Lemmas 6.16–6.17 was checked; it gives the slightly stronger saving (n − 2)/((n + 1)(2n² + 7n + 2)), so the printed bound holds. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.19–6.21, 6.23 and Proposition 6.22 (shallow cusp, K_1 ⊂ Z)
items.statement: If K_1 ⊂ Z and I(K_1, s) ≫ X^{−δ}, the s_i satisfy (52) (Lemma 6.19). If moreover the full count ≫ X^{n+1−δ}, then s_i ≪ Y^{258g³δ} for i ≥ g + 3 (53) (Lemma 6.20). Suppose M > X^η, δ < min(η, 1)/(1355g⁶), and (52)–(53) hold. Then imposing det B = 0 and |q| > M gives #((s(YD) × s(YD)) ∩ L(M))δ(s) ≪ X^{n+1+514g³δ−1/2} (Lemma 6.21). The key input is Lemma 6.23: if b_{g+1,g+1} = b_{g+1,g+2} = b_{g+2,g+2} = 0, then |q| ≪ X^{1355g⁶δ}. With δ = 64min(η, 1)/(1355n⁶), N ≪ X^{n+1−64min(η,1)/(1355n⁶)} (Proposition 6.22).
items.locator: §6.3.2–6.3.3, Lemmas 6.19–6.21, 6.23, Proposition 6.22 and proofs, pp.36–43, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprints E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.11 (shallow cusp, even n)
items.statement: If M > X^η with η > 0, then I^scusp_X(L(M)) = O(X^{n+1−min(η,1)/(22n⁶)}), from Propositions 6.18 and 6.22 (applied with η = 1/4 in §6.5).
items.locator: Theorem 6.11, p.33, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 6.25 (corrected: lower bound for det(B^top(B^top)^t))
items.statement: For (A, B) ∈ (YD × YD) ∩ W_0(R), W = W_{n+1}, Δ is homogeneous of degree 2n(n + 1), so |Δ(Y^{−1}(A, B))| = X^{−2n}|Δ(A, B)|. With the corrected Proposition 3.6: if |Δ(A, B)| > X^{2n−κ″}, then det(B^top(B^top)^t) ≫ Y^{2(g+1)}X^{−2κ″}. The printed version assumes only |Δ(A, B)| > X^{2n−2−κ} and concludes det(B^top(B^top)^t) ≫ Y^{2(g+1)−(n+1)κ}; that does not follow (E3).
items.locator: Lemma 6.25 and proof, p.44, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E3)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 6.26 (upper bound for |q| in the deep cusp)
items.statement: For saturated Z ⊂ Z_1 containing a_{g+1,g+1} and ℓ_{g+1,g+1}, s ∈ T_Z(L, Y) and (A, B) ∈ (s(YD) × s(YD)) ∩ L(1): |q|(A, B) ≪ Y^{(g+1)(g+2)}L_1⋯L_{g+1}/det(B_0^top(B_0^top)^t)^{1/2}, with (A_0, B_0) = s^{−1}(A, B) (from (69)–(71)). With the printed Lemma 6.25 this is ≪ Y^{(g+1)²+(n+1)κ/2}∏_{i≤g+1}L_i (66). With the corrected Lemma 6.25 (E3), after discarding forms with small |f(0, 1)|, it is ≪ Y^{(g+1)²}X^{κ″}∏_{i≤g+1}L_i.
items.locator: Proposition 6.26 and proof, pp.45–47, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E3)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.24 (deep cusp, even n)
items.statement: I^dcusp_X(L(M)) = O(X^{n+1+κ/2}log^{2n}X/M). Proof: bound #(s(YD) ∩ S(Z)) by (73) and #(s(YD) ∩ S(L, s)) by (76)–(78), and impose M ≪ Y^{(g+1)²+(n+1)κ/2}∏L_i (75). With the repair of E3 the exponent κ/2 becomes κ″ = κn/(n − 1).
items.locator: Theorem 6.24 and proof, pp.44–50, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E3)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5(a) (tail estimate, strongly divisible case)
items.statement: For n ≥ 3, M > 0 and ε > 0: #⋃_{m>M sqfree}{f ∈ W^{(1)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n+1+ε}/M + X^n), by the quantitative Ekedahl sieve.
items.locator: Theorem 5(a), p.3; §6.5, p.50, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5(b) (tail estimate, weakly divisible case, odd n)
items.statement: For odd n ≥ 3: #⋃_{m>M sqfree}{f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n+1+ε}/M + X^{n+1−1/(2n)+ε}), from (14), (16) and Theorem 4.2.
items.locator: Theorem 5(b), p.3; §6.5, p.50, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (gap E6)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5(c) (tail estimate, weakly divisible case, even n)
items.statement: For even n ≥ 4: #⋃_{m>M sqfree}{f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : H(f) < X} = O(X^{n+1+ξ}/√M + X^{n+1−1/(88n⁶)}), with ξ = 1/(88n⁵) as printed. With the repair of E3, ξ = 1/(44n⁵). Proof (§6.5): for m ≤ X^{1/2}, #{f ∈ W^{(2)}_m, H < X} ≪ X^{n+1}/m^{2−ε}, so one may assume M > X^{1/2}; then (35), (37), Lemmas 6.1–6.2 and Theorems 6.6, 6.11, 6.24 with κ = (2n − 2)/(88n⁶).
items.locator: Theorem 5(c), p.4; §6.5, p.50, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (errors E3, E4; gap E6; misprint E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 6.27 (uniformity for m² | Δ)
items.statement: For n ≥ 3: Σ_{m>M sqfree}#{f ∈ W_m : H(f) < X} ≪_ε X^{n+1+ξ_n+ε}/M^{δ_n} + X^{n+1−η_n+ε}, with δ_n = 1/2, ξ_n = 0, η_n = 1/(2n) for odd n and δ_n = 1/3, ξ_n = 1/(88n⁵), η_n = 1/(88n⁶) for even n. Proof: split m = m_1m_2 (strong and weak primes) and take M_1 = M_2 = √M (n odd) or M_1 = M^{1/3}, M_2 = M^{2/3} (n even).
items.locator: Corollary 6.27 and proof, p.51, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10; ξ_n for even n per E3)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (squarefree sieve with conditions at p | N)
items.statement: For squarefree N and nonempty Σ_p ⊂ V_n(Z/p²Z) (p | N): #{f ∈ V_n(Σ) : H(f) < X, Δ(f) squarefree} = α_n(Σ)(2X)^{n+1} + O_ε(E(X, N, ε)), and likewise for R_f maximal with β_n(Σ). Here E = X^{n+1−η_n+ε} + N²X^{n+3(η_n+ξ_n)+ε} + N^{2n+2}X^{(6n+3)(η_n+ξ_n)+ε}. Proof: inclusion–exclusion over m ≤ M = X^{3η_n+3ξ_n} coprime to N, with Corollary 6.27 for the tail. Theorem 6 is N = 1.
items.locator: Theorem 7.1 and proof, pp.51–52, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (gap E11)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1 (density of squarefree discriminants; corrected for n = 4)
items.statement: For n ≥ 2, when integral binary n-ic forms are ordered by H, the density with squarefree discriminant exists and equals α_n = ∏_pα_n(p): (1/2)∏_{p>2}(1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p − 1/p³) ≈ 38.97% (n = 2); (3/8)∏_{p>2}(1 − 1/p)²(1 + 1/p)² ≈ 24.64% (n = 3); and (3/8)∏_{p>2}(1 − 1/p)²(1 + 1/p)(1 + 1/p − 1/p²) ≈ 20.83% for every n ≥ 4. The printed n = 4 value, (3/8)∏(1 − 1/p)²(1 + 2/p − 2/p⁴ + 1/p⁵) ≈ 21.18%, is wrong (E1).
items.locator: Theorem 1, p.2; §7, p.52; Appendix, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E1, gap E8)
items.note: Constants computed with PARI prodeulerrat: 0.389743, 0.246384, 0.208276 (corrected n = 4 and n ≥ 5), and 0.211795 (printed n = 4). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2 (density of maximal R_f)
items.statement: For n ≥ 2, among irreducible integral binary n-ic forms ordered by H, the density with R_f the maximal order is ∏_p(1 − 1/p² − 1/p³ + 1/p⁴) ≈ 53.59% (n = 2), and ζ(2)^{−1}ζ(3)^{−1} ≈ 50.57% for n ≥ 3.
items.locator: Theorem 2, pp.2–3; §7, p.52, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (gap E8)

items.name: Theorem 6 (power-saving counts)
items.statement: With η_n = 1/(2n) for odd n and 1/(88n⁶) for even n: #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X, Δ(f) squarefree} = α_n(2X)^{n+1} + O_ε(X^{n+1−η_n+ε}), and #{f : H(f) < X, R_f maximal} = β_n(2X)^{n+1} + O_ε(X^{n+1−η_n+ε}). Analogues hold with finitely many local conditions (including at infinity) that do not force emptiness.
items.locator: Theorem 6, p.4; §7, p.52, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The arithmetic Bertini theorem for P¹_Z (Poonen's conjecture)
items.statement: Poonen conjectured that for a quasiprojective X ⊂ P^N_Z, regular of dimension m, the density of hyperplane sections that are regular of dimension m − 1 is ζ_X(m + 1)^{−1} ([28, §5]). Theorem 2 proves this, unconditionally, for X = P¹_Z embedded by binary n-ic forms with the box ordering: ζ_{P¹_Z}(s) = ζ(s)ζ(s − 1), so the density is ζ(2)^{−1}ζ(3)^{−1}, for every fixed n ≥ 3 and not only as n → ∞.
items.locator: §1, p.3, citing [28, §5 and Theorem 5.1], Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (misprint E10)
items.note: Poonen's abc-conditional result is [28, Theorem 5.1]. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Minkowski-reduced bases
items.statement: A Z-basis of a lattice is Minkowski-reduced if each successive vector is a shortest vector extending the previous ones to part of a basis; a lattice generically has a unique such basis up to signs.
items.locator: §7, p.52, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Also an item of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Minkowski-reduced, quasi-reduced and strongly quasi-reduced binary forms
items.statement: For a real binary n-ic form f with a_0 ≠ 0 and Δ(f) ≠ 0, R_f is the lattice in R[x]/(f(x, 1)) ≅ R^n spanned by 1, ζ_1 = a_0θ, …, ζ_{n−1} = a_0θ^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_{n−1}θ. f is Minkowski-reduced if this basis is Minkowski-reduced, quasi-reduced if γ·f is Minkowski-reduced for some γ ∈ SL_2(Z), and "strongly" if moreover R_f has a unique Minkowski-reduced basis (necessarily up to sign).
items.locator: §7, p.52, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 7.2 (corrected: rings of strongly quasi-reduced forms)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and f, f* be strongly quasi-reduced integral binary n-ic forms with R_f ≅ R_{f*}. Then f* is GL_2(Z)-equivalent to f (f* ∈ SL_2(Z)·{f, f(−x, y)}), but not necessarily SL_2(Z)-equivalent as printed (E5).
items.locator: Lemma 7.2 and proof, pp.52–53, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E5)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3 (S_n-fields of degree n)
items.statement: For n ≥ 3, the number of isomorphism classes of degree-n number fields with Galois group S_n and |Disc| < X is ≫ X^{1/2+1/(n−1)}; they may be taken with squarefree discriminant. Proof: take a small open B of strongly quasi-reduced forms of discriminant ≤ 1 with no two elements equivalent (GL_2(Z)-equivalent, by the correction E5); apply the sieve to B_X = X^{1/(2n−2)}·B, which contains ≫ X^{(n+1)/(2n−2)} maximal (squarefree-discriminant) forms; Lemma 7.2 makes their fields distinct.
items.locator: Theorem 3, p.3; proof, p.53, Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025), e17 (error E5, gap E11)
items.note: This improves X^{1/2+1/n} of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4 (unramified A_n-extensions of quadratic fields; Nakagawa resurrected)
items.statement: For n ≥ 3, the total number of unramified A_n-extensions of real (resp. imaginary) quadratic fields F with |Disc(F)| < X is ≫ X^{(n+1)/(2n−2)}. The retracted results [24, Theorems 3–4] and [26, Theorem 2] of Nakagawa hold, since the missing ingredient was a tail estimate like Theorem 5.

routes.reason: GN.4 owns lattice-point estimates, and RS-07 makes ST.2 consume it for the generic counts. That covers Davenport's lemma, Schmidt's bound by successive minima, and the new bound (§5) for singular symmetric matrices in skewed boxes. The last is a simplified, skew-uniform version of Eskin–Katznelson's upper bound, built from the lattices S′(Λ) of fixed row space.
GN.3 owns reduction domains. Minkowski-reduced bases and their uniqueness up to sign underlie the quasi-reduction of §7, as in PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22.

SV.2 owns large-sieve inequalities. Proposition 4.3 is the multidimensional arithmetic large sieve for lattice points in boxes (Huxley, Kowalski) and its corollary when a positive proportion of classes is excluded at every prime, which drives the main-body estimates (Propositions 4.4 and 6.9).

IG.2 owns Hilbert irreducibility. Kuba's count of reducible binary forms is a quantitative form of it, used in (14) and (35). The corresponding Dietmann bound of PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22 is routed to the same stage.

The error enters only through the ν_1(4, p) term of subset 1. For n ≥ 5 the terms ν_1(n) + ν_1(n − 1)/p combine to (1 − 1/p)²/p with either exponent, so those formulas are right. sourceIssues.printed: "Proposition 3.6. We have det(A^top(A^top)^t) det(B^top(B^top)^t) | Δ as elements in Z[W_0]." Proof: "Suppose (A, B) ∈ W_0(C) with det(B^top(B^top)^t) = 0. Then B^top does not have full rank."
sourceIssues.correction: Over C, det(MM^t) = 0 does not imply rank M < g (for M = (1, i), MM^t = 0), so the Nullstellensatz argument fails and the statement is false. What the argument does prove: Δ vanishes on the complex locus where B^top (or A^top) has rank < g. So Δ lies in the ideal generated by the g × g minors of B^top (a prime determinantal ideal), and likewise for A^top. On bounded sets this gives |Δ| ≪ Σ|minors| ≪ det(B^top(B^top)^t)^{1/2}, by Cauchy–Binet, and that suffices for Lemma 6.25 with the exponent doubled.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample for n = 3 (g = 1): A = [[0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 1]] and B = [[0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0], [1, 0, 0]] lie in W_0(Z). Then f_{A,B} = −y(x² − 3xy + y²) and Δ = 5, while det(A^top(A^top)^t)det(B^top(B^top)^t) = 1·2 = 2 ∤ 5. At random integral points the claimed divisibility held in only 6 of 37 cases for n = 3 and 0 of 40 for n = 5. Δ vanished at all 12 random points with rank-1 B^top for n = 5.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 7.2 and proof, pp.52–53; proof of Theorem 3, p.53
sourceIssues.printed: "Lemma 7.2 … Suppose the corresponding rank-n rings R_f and R_{f*} are isomorphic. Then f(x, y) and f*(x, y) are SL_2(Z)-equivalent. Proof. … By the uniqueness of Minkowski-reduced bases, φ must map the basis elements 1, ζ_1, …, ζ_{n−1} for R_f to the corresponding basis elements 1, ζ*_1, …, ζ*_{n−1}."
sourceIssues.correction: Minkowski-reduced bases are unique at best up to the signs of their vectors, so φ(ζ_i) = ±ζ*_i. The conclusion is only that f* is GL_2(Z)-equivalent to f, e.g. f*(x, y) = f(−x, y). In the proof of Theorem 3, choose B so that no two of its elements are GL_2(Z)-equivalent (GL_2(Z) also acts discretely). The bound is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample for n = 3: f = x³ − x²y + xy² + y³, an S_3 cubic (disc −44), is strongly Minkowski-reduced. An exhaustive search gives the reduced basis 1, ζ_1, ζ_2 with unique minima up to sign. f*(x, y) = f(−x, y) = −x³ − x²y − xy² + y³ has the same lattice R_{f*} = R_f, since ζ*_i = ±ζ_i, so it is strongly Minkowski-reduced too. But f* is not SL_2(Z)-equivalent to f. Otherwise f would have a stabilizer element δ of determinant −1, and −δ would be a nontrivial automorphism of R_f in the twisted GL_2(Z)-action, which is impossible for an order in a non-Galois cubic field. Part I's Lemma 5.1 has the same sign gap (its E10).
